fieldValues.title: Alt text and caption on essay images
fieldValues.decision_question: Must an image paragraph carry alt text, and what form does its caption take?
fieldValues.context: The owner asked for a caption (vignette 02e02668). Alt text is what a screen reader and a text-only export read in place of the image. The essay's agents never write essay text (srs-context decision 82fbca88), so alt text is the writer's.
fieldValues.friction: An image without a text equivalent is invisible to some readers and to every text projection of the essay, including search.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Alt text required, caption optional plain text (recommended). For: accessible by default; the caption cannot carry a markdown image, so it stays outside the image route. Against: one required field to fill.
B. Both optional. For: fastest. Against: images without text equivalents.
C. Caption as markdown. For: links and emphasis in captions. Against: another markdown surface to police for images.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Accessible to screen readers; searchable; no second route for images.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Every essay image carries alt text written by the writer, and its caption, when present, is plain text.
fieldValues.rationale: Alt text is an accessibility basic and the essay's text projection depends on it; a plain-text caption keeps markdown images out.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers ask for links or emphasis in captions, or the alt text field is mostly filled with filler.
